- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, reduce forecast overshoot by 5–15% to avoid overreacting to short-term momentum.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and price is trending up, cap forecast gains to prevent false optimism.  
- When model forecast spikes sharply after a low, reduce the peak by 10–20% to account for mean reversion or volatility decay.  
- If true outcome consistently lags forecast by 1–3 days, adjust forward-looking models to slightly under-predict early peaks.  
- For 30-day horizons, if forecast mean is >10% above recent 18-day average, apply downward bias correction proportional to sentiment volatility.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, smooth forecast transitions to avoid abrupt directional shifts.
